meta.label: defaults
meta.seed_rule: run i of scenario S uses seed + i*7919 + crc32(S) % 100000

profile.name: defaults
profile.description: Code defaults: no voice setting overridden.
profile.source: app/config.py at the benchmarked revision. Every VOICE_* variable in the calling shell is cleared before Settings load.
profile.verify_with: results.json meta.effective_flags lists what the revision resolved.

model_notes: Real: every Pipecat processor between the socket and the providers, exactly as build_pipecat_voice_task wires it (utterance gate, transcript relay, speculative prefetch/generation, Flux turn strategies incl. backchannel grace window, Cognitive LLM bridge with deep ack and tool narration, interrupt reporter with stop marker and played-audio reconciliation, Pipecat TTS audio contexts and word timestamps, websocket output pacing, spoken-text tap, durable persistence and the barge-in write gate).

Scripted STT follows Pipecat 1.12 Deepgram Flux frame semantics: StartOfTurn, EagerEndOfTurn/TurnResumed, EndOfTurn with finalized transcript. Flux 1.12 pushes no interim transcripts, so none are sent (as in production). Flux's own end-of-turn decision is a fixed, jittered delay after speech ends, not a model of its confidence.

Fake TTS is shaped like the ElevenLabs websocket service (one context per reply, first-byte delay, faster-than-real-time streaming, flush/close). Audio is a constant tone whose sample value encodes the segment, so labels survive re-chunking. Provider-side late frames are modelled; ElevenLabs alignment quirks are not.

Brain is scripted (first-token delay, streamed tokens, tool calls, failures, governed writes checked with the real raise_if_barge_in_blocks_invoke). It does not model the real CognitiveTurnKernel, model routing or tool selection; the plans are fixed per scenario.

Browser model reproduces use-voice-duplex-session.ts drop rules (reply_id <= interrupted id, flush on speech.interrupted) and the voice-pcm-jitter.ts lead (120 ms initial, +60 ms per mid-reply underrun, max 320 ms). It does not model the client-side bargeIn() path (the server does not relay interim transcripts), the HTTP fallback watchdog, or AudioContext scheduling jitter.

NOT modelled: acoustics, microphone echo and echo cancellation, real Deepgram/ElevenLabs/model latency distributions, network latency/jitter/loss (network_s=0), CPU load (virtual time makes processing free), multi-worker Redis stop markers (in-process fallback), and the read-only prefetch services (counted, not run).
Virtual clock: asyncio timers and time.time/monotonic/perf_counter are virtual; worker threads take zero virtual time. Results are deterministic for a given seed and code version.

S1.title: long pause / incomplete thought
S1.description: User: "I want to check... [1.2 s pause] ...last month's traffic". Flux emits EagerEndOfTurn in the pause and TurnResumed when speech resumes (the turn is not committed).
S1.expected: No bot audio during the pause; one answer about last month.

S1b.title: long pause, STT commits early
S1b.description: Same words, but Flux commits EndOfTurn on "I want to check" during the 1.2 s pause; the rest arrives as a new turn.
S1b.expected: Ideally no audible reply to the fragment; the full request answered once.

S2.title: backchannel during playback
S2.description: User asks for traffic; 1.5 s into the spoken answer says "Mm-hmm." (0.4 s).
S2.expected: Bot keeps speaking; no new turn; history = full answer.

S2b.title: backchannel "Yeah." (control)
S2b.description: As S2 with "Yeah.", a word the utterance gate does not drop.

S3.title: correction before speech starts
S3.description: User: "show me traffic for last week, no, last month" with a 0.35 s hesitation after "week".
S3.expected: One answer about last month; nothing about last week is spoken.

S4.title: correction after speech starts (barge-in)
S4.description: User asks for last week's traffic; 1.2 s into the answer barges in: "use last quarter instead".
S4.expected: Old answer stops quickly; new answer about last quarter; history holds only what was heard.

S5.title: repeated interruptions then resumed request
S5.description: Pipeline summary request; user cuts in with "wait" 1 s into the answer, then "actually hold on" while the bot answers that, then "okay go on, give me the pipeline summary".
S5.expected: Each cut-in silences the bot; the final request gets the summary once.

S6.title: late TTS audio after cancellation
S6.description: As S4, but the TTS provider keeps emitting the cancelled context's audio for 300 ms after close.
S6.expected: No frame of the cancelled reply is played after the interruption.

S7.title: slow tool (4 s)
S7.description: "pull the pipeline report for this quarter": one CRM tool call taking 4 s.
S7.expected: Progress narration covers the wait; answer after the tool.

S7b.title: failed tool
S7b.description: "what was our website traffic last month": the analytics tool fails after 1.5 s.
S7b.expected: Failure narrated honestly; no invented numbers.

S8.title: approval "yes... wait"
S8.description: Bot drafts an email and asks to send; user says "yes", pauses ~0.5 s, says "wait". Flux may commit "yes" on the pause.
S8.expected: No email is sent (the final intent is "wait").

S9.title: complex reasoning turn (deep tier)
S9.description: Multi-part analysis request; brain thinks 2.5 s, runs two tools (1.5 s, 1.0 s), thinks 1.5 s, then answers.
S9.expected: Early acknowledgement and progress narration; answer when ready.

S10.title: "stop talking, keep working"
S10.description: During a 6 s CRM task, while progress narration plays, the user says "stop talking, keep working".
S10.expected: Ideal: narration stops, the task keeps running and its result is delivered. (No dedicated path in current code.)

S11.title: "cancel it" during a running task
S11.description: An approved CRM batch write is running (user: "yes, go ahead and move them all"; the provider call is made 4 s into a 5 s tool call). 0.5 s into the progress narration the user says "cancel it".
S11.expected: The task stops and the write is not committed. (Cancellation rides on barge-in + stop marker.)

S12.title: reconnect mid-reply (socket drop)
S12.description: 1.5 s into the spoken traffic answer the socket drops; 1 s later a new socket opens on the same conversation and the user asks what was said last.
S12.expected: Durable history (and the brain's view of it after reconnect) holds only what was heard.

S13.title: "why?" during a running task (answer-first)
S13.description: "pull the pipeline report for this quarter" runs a 6 s CRM tool; 0.5 s into the first narration line (or 2.5 s after the request if nothing narrates) the user asks a bare "why?". Interacts with voice_interrupt_intents_v1 + voice_explain_aside_v1 + voice_answer_first_v1.
S13.expected: The question is answered while the task keeps running; the task's result is then spoken exactly once, and no narration line plays after the result starts.

S13b.title: "why is it taking so long" during a running task
S13b.description: As S13, with a question the interrupt-intent classifier reads as an explanation request.
S13b.expected: The question is answered while the task keeps running; the task's result is then spoken exactly once, and no narration line plays after the result starts.

S14.title: explain aside + playback-grounded history
S14.description: As S13b; after everything is quiet the user asks "okay, and how many open deals was that". Checks what history stores (voice_playback_grounded_history_v1): the follow-up's brain history and the durable rows.
S14.expected: History holds the aside and the task's result, both as heard and in the order heard; nothing unheard is stored; the follow-up sees both.

S15.title: explain request cuts the answer (grounded history)
S15.description: 1.5 s into the spoken traffic answer the user asks "wait, what does that mean" (no task running: the explanation interrupts the answer). Interacts with voice_interrupt_intents_v1 + voice_playback_grounded_history_v1.
S15.expected: The answer stops; the explanation is spoken; the explanation's brain history and the stored answer hold only what was heard.

S16.title: bare "stop" over the answer (ducking)
S16.description: 1.5 s into the spoken traffic answer the user says "stop". Interacts with voice_interrupt_intents_v1 (a bare stop is a full stop) + voice_overlap_duck_v1 (duck while the words are classified).
S16.expected: The answer is cut and stays cut: never restored to full level, not restarted; at most a short acknowledgement.

S17.title: backchannel "Right, okay." (ducking)
S17.description: As S2 with a two-word backchannel. Interacts with voice_interrupt_intents_v1 (BACKCHANNEL keeps the reply) + voice_overlap_duck_v1 (duck while classifying, then unduck).
S17.expected: Bot keeps speaking; if it ducked, the reply is restored (unduck); no new turn.

S18.title: correction while ducked ("no, I meant last month")
S18.description: User asks for last week's traffic; 1.2 s into the answer says "no, I meant last month". Interacts with voice_interrupt_intents_v1 (CORRECTION revises the request) + voice_overlap_duck_v1.
S18.expected: The old answer is cut (never restored to full level); the new answer is about last month; nothing about last week after the cut.
